name: Cloudflare MCP Server Portals
tagline: Zero Trust feature that puts many remote MCP servers behind one endpoint with SSO, access policies and logs.
bestFor: Teams already using Cloudflare One or Cloudflare Access
description: MCP server portals are part of Cloudflare One. A portal groups several remote MCP servers behind one URL, signs users in through Cloudflare Access and lets admins turn individual tools and prompts on or off. Portals became generally available on September 24, 2026. Cloudflare One is free for up to 50 users and costs $7 per user per month on Pay-as-you-go.
pros: Cloudflare One Free plan covers up to 50 users
Per-portal tool and prompt allowlists, plus aliases to rename tools
Logs each tool call with time, status, server and duration
Optional Gateway routing adds HTTP logging and DLP scanning
cons: Only remote HTTP MCP servers are supported; stdio servers must be put behind HTTP first
Logpush export of portal logs requires an Enterprise plan
Pricing pages do not mention portals, so per-plan feature limits are unclear
freePlanDetails: Cloudflare One Free plan: $0 for up to 50 users. Cloudflare says portals are available to all customers; the pricing page does not list portal limits per plan.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: Cloudflare One (Zero Trust) Free plan, up to 50 users.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.notes: Per user per month. The pricing page does not list an annual price for this plan.

plans.name: Contract
plans.notes: Custom annual price per user. Logpush export of portal logs is Enterprise-only.

integrations: Any remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP or SSE; up to 120 servers per portal

name: Zuplo MCP Gateway
tagline: Managed proxy in the Zuplo API gateway that fronts remote MCP servers with OAuth, role-based tool access and audit logs.
bestFor: API teams that want MCP access control in the same gateway as their APIs
description: Zuplo MCP Gateway puts one or more remote MCP servers behind a single OAuth-protected endpoint. It stores per-user upstream tokens, filters which tools, prompts and resources each role sees, and logs every tool call against the end user. It entered public beta on June 2, 2026 and became generally available in the August 2026 changelog. Zuplo lists only an Enterprise plan with custom pricing.
pros: Capability Filter exposes a curated set of tools per route, user, role or group
Per-user upstream credentials; raw upstream tokens never reach the AI client
Works with identity providers such as Auth0, Okta and Microsoft Entra
Runs on managed edge, managed dedicated or self-hosted deployments
cons: No public prices or free plan; only a custom Enterprise plan is listed
SSO, role-based access and self-hosting are priced as add-ons
Docs cover remote MCP servers only
trial: Free trial on request through sales

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Annual contract quoted on request volume, SLA and add-ons. Includes 1 million requests per month and MCP Gateway. SSO and role-based access, observability integrations and self-hosted options are add-ons.

integrations: Server library with upstreams such as Stripe, Linear, GitHub and PostHog, plus custom remote servers

sources.label: Zuplo changelog: MCP Gateway public beta

launch.what: MCP Gateway moved from public beta (June 2, 2026) to general availability, adding role-based tool access and audit logging.

name: Speakeasy MCP Gateway
tagline: Usage-billed MCP gateway with IdP sign-in, tool-level permissions and per-call audit logs.
bestFor: Companies giving employees governed access to MCP servers across many AI clients
description: Speakeasy MCP Gateway, the successor to Speakeasy's Gram platform, went live on March 10, 2026. Employees sign in through their identity provider, roles from IdP groups decide which servers and tools each person gets, and every tool call is logged with user, client, tool, arguments and result. Pay-as-you-go has no platform fee and bills usage, including $20 per GiB of MCP gateway egress.
pros: No platform fee on Pay-as-you-go; billed only for usage
Tool-level allowlists per server and roles synced from the IdP
Audit logs stream to Datadog, Splunk, Grafana or any OTLP collector
Detects and blocks unapproved MCP servers by default
cons: Usage pricing makes monthly cost hard to predict
SSO and the full audit trail are listed under Enterprise
Free trial length is not stated
trial: Free trial; length not stated. Adding a payment method converts to Pay-as-you-go.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.notes: No platform fee; usage billed monthly. Agent session storage $0.35 per 1M tokens, risk scanning $0.99 per 1M tokens scanned, MCP gateway egress $20 per GiB. Inference billed at provider cost.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Annual contract priced on tokens under management. Includes SSO, full audit trail, SLA-backed support with a forward-deployed engineer and concierge onboarding.

integrations: Pre-built connectors including GitHub, Notion, Linear, Stripe, HubSpot and PagerDuty, plus your own servers
support: Dedicated support channel and forward-deployed engineer (Enterprise)

name: Metorial
tagline: Open-source MCP and skills gateway that gives each employee one MCP URL for approved integrations.
bestFor: Teams that want a self-hostable gateway with a large integration catalog
description: Metorial is a Y Combinator Fall 2025 company from Vienna. Each user gets one MCP URL that connects their AI client to the integrations and tools they are allowed to use, with managed OAuth, per-tool read, write or off settings and logs of every call. The platform is open source under Apache 2.0. A free Dev plan includes 500,000 tool calls per month, and Scale costs $250 per month.
pros: Free Dev plan includes 500,000 tool calls per month and unlimited auth connections
Open source under Apache 2.0 and self-hostable
1,000+ integrations, plus internal and third-party remote servers
Per-tool read, write or off permissions by person and group
cons: RBAC, SAML SSO, on-prem deployment and SOC 2 are listed under Enterprise
Dev plan allows 2 team members, 10 provider integrations and one project
freePlanDetails: Metorial Dev: $0, 500,000 tool calls and 10,000 callbacks per month, unlimited auth connections, up to 2 team members, up to 10 provider integrations, one environment and one project, 30-day log retention; no card required.

plans.name: Metorial Dev
plans.notes: 500,000 tool calls and 10,000 callbacks per month; up to 2 team members and 10 provider integrations; 30-day log retention.

plans.name: Metorial Scale
plans.notes: 2,500,000 tool calls and 100,000 callbacks per month; 90-day log retention. Overage $1 per 1,500 tool calls and $1 per 750 callbacks.

plans.notes: Custom limits, on-prem deployment, SOC 2 Type II and GDPR, RBAC, SAML/SSO and IAM, Slack or Teams support with SLA.

support: Slack or Teams support with SLA (Enterprise)
